_**Agent (model claude-4-sonnet, mode Agent)**_

I'll help you create a PowerShell command to rename/replace a given string in each file within a directory with another string. Let me provide you with a comprehensive solution.

Here's the PowerShell command to replace a string in all files within a directory:

```powershell
Get-ChildItem -Path "C:\path\to\directory" -File -Recurse | ForEach-Object {
    (Get-Content $_.FullName) -replace 'old_string', 'new_string' | Set-Content $_.FullName
}
```

Here's a breakdown of the components:

## Basic Command Structure

```powershell
# Replace string in all files in current directory (non-recursive)
Get-ChildItem -File | ForEach-Object {
    (Get-Content $_.FullName) -replace 'old_string', 'new_string' | Set-Content $_.FullName
}

# Replace string in all files in specific directory (recursive)
Get-ChildItem -Path "C:\your\directory\path" -File -Recurse | ForEach-Object {
    (Get-Content $_.FullName) -replace 'old_string', 'new_string' | Set-Content $_.FullName
}
```

## More Advanced Examples

### 1. Filter by file extension:
```powershell
Get-ChildItem -Path "C:\path\to\directory" -Filter "*.txt" -Recurse | ForEach-Object {
    (Get-Content $_.FullName) -replace 'old_string', 'new_string' | Set-Content $_.FullName
}
```

### 2. Multiple file extensions:
```powershell
Get-ChildItem -Path "C:\path\to\directory" -Include "*.txt", "*.py", "*.md" -Recurse | ForEach-Object {
    (Get-Content $_.FullName) -replace 'old_string', 'new_string' | Set-Content $_.FullName
}
```

### 3. Case-insensitive replacement:
```powershell
Get-ChildItem -Path "C:\path\to\directory" -File -Recurse | ForEach-Object {
    (Get-Content $_.FullName) -ireplace 'old_string', 'new_string' | Set-Content $_.FullName
}
```

### 4. With backup and error handling:
```powershell
Get-ChildItem -Path "C:\path\to\directory" -File -Recurse | ForEach-Object {
    try {
        $content = Get-Content $_.FullName -Raw
        if ($content -match 'old_string') {
            # Create backup
            Copy-Item $_.FullName "$($_.FullName).bak"
            # Replace content
            $content -replace 'old_string', 'new_string' | Set-Content $_.FullName
            Write-Host "Replaced in: $($_.Name)"
        }
    }
    catch {
        Write-Error "Error processing $($_.Name): $($_.Exception.Message)"
    }
}
```

### 5. Using regex patterns:
```powershell
Get-ChildItem -Path "C:\path\to\directory" -File -Recurse | ForEach-Object {
    (Get-Content $_.FullName) -replace '\bold_string\b', 'new_string' | Set-Content $_.FullName
}
```

## One-liner for Quick Use

```powershell
# Replace in current directory
ls -File | %{(gc $_.FullName) -replace 'old','new' | sc $_.FullName}

# Replace in specific directory recursively  
ls "C:\path" -File -R | %{(gc $_.FullName) -replace 'old','new' | sc $_.FullName}
```

## Parameters Explanation:
- `-Path`: Specifies the directory path
- `-File`: Only gets files (not directories)
- `-Recurse`: Searches subdirectories
- `-Filter` or `-Include`: Filters by file pattern
- `-replace`: Case-sensitive replacement
- `-ireplace`: Case-insensitive replacement
- `Get-Content`: Reads file content
- `Set-Content`: Writes content back to file

**Important Notes:**
1. Always test on a backup or small subset first
2. The command modifies files in place
3. Use `-Raw` parameter with `Get-Content` for better performance on large files
4. Consider creating backups before running on important files

_**Agent (model claude-4-sonnet, mode Agent)**_

Yes! You can also rename folders (directories) that contain a specific string. Here are the commands to handle both files AND folders:

## Your Current Command (Files Only)
Your command only handles file contents:

```powershell
Get-ChildItem -Path "C:\Users\RAVEN\AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\Signatures" -File -Recurse | ForEach-Object {
    (Get-Content $_.FullName) -replace 'ali.maung@rolls-royce.com', 'ali.maung001@outlook.com' | Set-Content $_.FullName
}
```

## Complete Solution: Files + Folders + File Contents

```powershell
$sourcePath = "C:\Users\RAVEN\AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\Signatures"
$oldString = "ali.maung@rolls-royce.com"
$newString = "ali.maung001@outlook.com"

# 1. Replace content in files
Get-ChildItem -Path $sourcePath -File -Recurse | ForEach-Object {
    (Get-Content $_.FullName) -replace $oldString, $newString | Set-Content $_.FullName
}

# 2. Rename files that contain the string in their names
Get-ChildItem -Path $sourcePath -File -Recurse | Where-Object { $_.Name -like "*$oldString*" } | ForEach-Object {
    $newName = $_.Name -replace [regex]::Escape($oldString), $newString
    Rename-Item -Path $_.FullName -NewName $newName
}

# 3. Rename folders that contain the string in their names (process deepest first)
Get-ChildItem -Path $sourcePath -Directory -Recurse | Sort-Object FullName -Descending | Where-Object { $_.Name -like "*$oldString*" } | ForEach-Object {
    $newName = $_.Name -replace [regex]::Escape($oldString), $newString
    Rename-Item -Path $_.FullName -NewName $newName
}
```

## One-Liner Version (All-in-One)

```powershell
$p="C:\Users\RAVEN\AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\Signatures";$o="ali.maung@rolls-royce.com";$n="ali.maung001@outlook.com";gci $p -File -R|%{(gc $_.FullName) -replace $o,$n|sc $_.FullName};gci $p -File -R|?{$_.Name -like "*$o*"}|%{ren $_.FullName ($_.Name -replace [regex]::Escape($o),$n)};gci $p -Directory -R|sort FullName -Desc|?{$_.Name -like "*$o*"}|%{ren $_.FullName ($_.Name -replace [regex]::Escape($o),$n)}
```

## Safer Version with Backup and Logging

```powershell
$sourcePath = "C:\Users\RAVEN\AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\Signatures"
$oldString = "ali.maung@rolls-royce.com"
$newString = "ali.maung001@outlook.com"

Write-Host "Starting replacement process..." -ForegroundColor Green

# 1. Replace content in files
Write-Host "Replacing content in files..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
Get-ChildItem -Path $sourcePath -File -Recurse | ForEach-Object {
    try {
        $content = Get-Content $_.FullName -Raw
        if ($content -match [regex]::Escape($oldString)) {
            # Create backup
            Copy-Item $_.FullName "$($_.FullName).bak"
            # Replace content
            $content -replace [regex]::Escape($oldString), $newString | Set-Content $_.FullName
            Write-Host "  Content replaced in: $($_.Name)" -ForegroundColor Cyan
        }
    }
    catch {
        Write-Error "Error processing file $($_.Name): $($_.Exception.Message)"
    }
}

# 2. Rename files
Write-Host "Renaming files..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
Get-ChildItem -Path $sourcePath -File -Recurse | Where-Object { $_.Name -like "*$oldString*" } | ForEach-Object {
    try {
        $newName = $_.Name -replace [regex]::Escape($oldString), $newString
        Rename-Item -Path $_.FullName -NewName $newName
        Write-Host "  File renamed: $($_.Name) -> $newName" -ForegroundColor Cyan
    }
    catch {
        Write-Error "Error renaming file $($_.Name): $($_.Exception.Message)"
    }
}

# 3. Rename folders (deepest first to avoid path issues)
Write-Host "Renaming folders..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
Get-ChildItem -Path $sourcePath -Directory -Recurse | Sort-Object FullName -Descending | Where-Object { $_.Name -like "*$oldString*" } | ForEach-Object {
    try {
        $newName = $_.Name -replace [regex]::Escape($oldString), $newString
        Rename-Item -Path $_.FullName -NewName $newName
        Write-Host "  Folder renamed: $($_.Name) -> $newName" -ForegroundColor Cyan
    }
    catch {
        Write-Error "Error renaming folder $($_.Name): $($_.Exception.Message)"
    }
}

Write-Host "Replacement process completed!" -ForegroundColor Green
```

## Key Points:

1. **File Contents**: Your original command handles this
2. **File Names**: Added file renaming for names containing the string
3. **Folder Names**: Added folder renaming (processed deepest-first to avoid path conflicts)
4. **Safety**: Uses `[regex]::Escape()` to handle special characters in email addresses
5. **Order**: Processes folders from deepest to shallowest to prevent path issues

The email address you're replacing contains special characters (@ and .) that need to be escaped in regex, which is why I used `[regex]::Escape()`.
